subject.title: feat(session): add named new and close chat commands

question: After the parser and proof gaps are fixed, should OpenClaw expose `/close` and `/delete` as chat-side commands that archive the active non-main session?
rationale: The code defect is mechanical, but adding destructive chat-side session commands is a user-facing session-state policy choice that tests alone cannot settle.

options.title: Accept after repair and proof
options.body: Keep `/close` and `/delete` if the parser is fixed, current-head proof shows non-main deletion and main-session refusal, and docs match the intended command contract.

options.title: Land naming only
options.body: Drop `/close` and `/delete` from this PR and keep session deletion owned by UI/gateway surfaces until a separate product decision is made.

options.title: Wait for title migration
options.body: Pause this PR until the canonical title/label migration lands, then rebase the naming path onto the approved session-name field.

recommendation.title: Accept after repair and proof
recommendation.body: Keep `/close` and `/delete` if the parser is fixed, current-head proof shows non-main deletion and main-session refusal, and docs match the intended command contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The affected `/new` reset-model behavior and product-level command contract history point to this owner as the best decision route.
